data.name: Ashit
data.gender_notes: Ashit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashit is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘asheshta’, meaning ‘eighth’. In Hindu mythology, the sun is considered the eighth deity and is symbolized by the god Surya. The name Ashit signifies the arrival of the morning sun, bringing new hope and energy. The name Ashit carries the meaning “Morning Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashit usually hope their child will grow to embody morning sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ashit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Morning Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashit total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Ashit, also known as Ashtavakra, was a sage and philosopher who is believed to have lived during the late Vedic period, around 600-500 BCE. He is best known for his teachings on the Upanishads, particularly the Chandogya Upanishad where he is depicted as a teacher to Janaka, the king of Videha. Ashtavakra's teachings emphasize the unity of all things and the importance of self-realization.

Ashit is also mentioned in the epic Mahabharata as the father of Amba, one of the five Pandava brothers' wives. Amba was in love with Bhima, but Bhima did not reciprocate her feelings. In her frustration, she cursed Bhima that he would marry her, but only after he had suffered great hardships. After Bhima's marriage to Draupadi, Amba was married to Bhima, fulfilling her curse. Bhima and Amba had no children together.
